answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so any gap or primary switch would raise delivery risk and is ruled out by the objective. Incumbent continuity previously kept integration and deliveries stable. They have refused a mid-cycle price reopen, but renewal is the moment prior cycles recovered margin via benchmarking and unlocked lower unit cost with a longer term without cutting scope. One decision should therefore be a renewal negotiation that trades term/volume for the mandated spend cut while keeping the incumbent as primary. Whether they will move after an explicit refusal this cycle is still uncertain; switch/second-source/defer remain uncommitted until that is tested.
